title: Postoperative early and long-term outcomes (morbidity, mortality) in chronic dialysis-dependent patients following cardiac surgery with a heart lung machine
summary: This study aims to investigate the short- and long-term outcomes of cardiac surgery in patients with chronic kidney disease requiring dialysis, focusing on the use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during the procedure. We seek to understand how surgery impacts morbidity and mortality in this vulnerable patient population, and whether newer, miniaturized CPB technologies (MiECC) can provide better outcomes. Findings from this research could improve clinical practices and enhance patient management strategies.
conditions: Other diseases of the heart or aorta that require a surgical intervention utilizing a heart lung machine

interventions.name: chronic dialysis-dependent patients who underwent cardiac surgery using a heart-lung machine  from 2006 to 2022.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Chronically dialysis-dependent patients (hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis) who underwent heart surgery using a heart lung machine (HLM) between 2006 and 2022.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who did not have chronic dialysis dependence before the heart surgery.
Patients who were operated without the use of a heart lung machine.
